spatial_claims.claim: SAS congruence (I.4) of triangles ABE and BCD: sides AB=BC, AE=CD, included angle A = angle C, yielding BE=BD and angle AEB = angle BDC
Triangle BDE is isosceles with BE=BD, so angle BDE = angle BED
Diagonal BD splits pentagon angle at D: angle CDE = angle BDC + angle BDE (ray DB between rays DC and DE)
Diagonal BE splits pentagon angle at E: angle DEA = angle AEB + angle BED (ray EB between rays EA and ED)
SAS congruence of triangles EAB and CBA: sides EA=BC, AB=BA, included angle A = angle B, yielding BE=CA
SAS congruence of triangles CDE and DEA: sides CD=DE, DE=EA, included angle D = angle E, yielding CE=DA and angle CED = angle DAE
SSS congruence (I.8) of triangles CEA and DAB: sides CE=DA, EA=AB, CA=BD, yielding angle CEA = angle DAB
Diagonal CE splits pentagon angle at E: angle DEA = angle DEC + angle CEA (ray EC between rays ED and EA)
Diagonal DA splits pentagon angle at A: angle EAB = angle EAD + angle DAB (ray AD between rays AE and AB)
SAS congruence of triangles EAB and CBA yielding BE=CA and angle AEB = angle BCA
SAS congruence of triangles EAB and CDE yielding BE=CE and angle ABE = angle DEC
Triangle ABE isosceles with AB=AE, so angle ABE = angle AEB
CA=CE (from BE=CA and BE=CE), so triangle ACE isosceles with angle CAE = angle CEA
Diagonal AC splits pentagon angle at A: angle EAB = angle EAC + angle CAB (ray AC between rays AE and AB)
Diagonals EC and EB split pentagon angle at E into three parts: angle DEA = angle DEC + angle CEB + angle BEA (angular order ED, EC, EB, EA)

configuration_map: Pentagon ABCDE is equilateral and convex with vertices in cyclic order A, B, C, D, E. All sides equal: AB=BC=CD=DE=EA. At each vertex, diagonals from that vertex pass through the pentagon interior and respect the cyclic angular ordering. At vertex D: angular order is DC, DB, DE. At vertex E: angular order is ED, EC, EB, EA. At vertex A: angular order is AE, AD, AC, AB. All angle decompositions (both two-way and three-way splits) respect these angular orderings. Key derived equalities: BE=BD (Step 1), BE=CA (Step 4), CE=DA (Step 5), CA=BD (chain from Steps 1,4). All congruence triangles (ABE/BCD, EAB/CBA, CDE/DEA, CEA/DAB, EAB/CDE) have properly matched sides and included angles.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. Every angle decomposition correctly places the splitting ray between the outer rays according to the convex pentagon's cyclic vertex ordering. All SAS and SSS congruence applications properly match sides and included angles. The two-case structure (consecutive and non-consecutive equal angles) is logically exhaustive, and the combinatorial claim that every non-consecutive triple has exactly one adjacent pair is verified. No contradictions found.
